work_order.understanding: This ticket collects eight review findings and one QA finding left over from PR #26 (issue #22), filed after that PR merged. Seven hold; the QA finding (/reports/spending spinning forever on the demo budget) does not reproduce and is dropped per the issue body's own instruction not to implement something that was never wrong. Dropping it dissolves the split question: the remaining seven findings are the review tail of one PR across four files. Two findings contradict each other as written — finding 1 wants the click path guarded like the keydown path, finding 5 says the guard finding 1 proposes would break every real click, and finding 5 is right. This version exists because v1 was rejected for three reasons, all about how the work order was written rather than what it proposed: two comment-text criteria marked verify:"test" with no CI case behind them; AC-5's named grep unable to fail on today's code because the phrase is wrapped across two lines; and a qa_script step asking QA to confirm the Calendar card's button does not navigate, which is the opposite of what that button is for. All three are now answered by measurement. Findings 2 and 3 are latent rather than live — no consumer reads status or isSuccess — but both are cheap to make true.
work_order.root_cause: PR #26 fixed a React validateDOMNesting warning by replacing the card's <Button> wrapper with a View carrying role="button". That removed the HTML-validity error but left the card's event handling two different shapes: the keydown path gained an explicit 'this press belongs to a descendant control, not the card' guard, while onClick stayed a bare goToReport. The two paths drifted because only one of them was given a rule. Findings 2 and 3 are a separate, smaller root cause: the isFirstLoad override was added as a targeted fix for id-less routes and shipped as a spread over the whole react-query result, so the object callers receive carries the derived flag next to the react-query fields the derivation deliberately contradicts, justified by a comment that misstates what it is.
work_order.approach:
Four files, all in packages/desktop-client/src. This version changes the plan in three places to answer the review's objections and leaves the rest of v1 intact.

Objection 1 — the two comment criteria become CI-provable. The schema's verify enum is browser|test|api; there is no review-scoped value, and qa.md:222-224 says a verify:"test" criterion is proven by CI and must cite "ci" in test_ids. So option (a) is unavailable and each comment criterion needs a real case in tests[]. The form matters, and I found it by running it: readFileSync(new URL('./ReportCard.tsx', import.meta.url), 'utf8') throws TypeError: The URL must be of scheme file under this vitest setup, so the idiomatic form is a trap. What works is path.resolve(import.meta.dirname, 'ReportCard.tsx'), which I verified resolves and reads the file's real content. Each of the three test files gains one case that reads its own sibling source this way and asserts on the comment, colocated with the module the comment describes rather than in a new grep-only file.

Objection 2 — AC-5's check now fails on today's code. The old grep for `react-query's own isLoading definition` cannot fail, because that phrase is split across useDashboardWidget.ts:22-23 by a line break and a `//` marker, so grep never sees it — the criterion would pass on unmodified code and would also pass if the implementer deleted the comment entirely. The replacement asserts on normalized text: strip `//` markers, collapse whitespace, then require that the normalized source mentions `isPending && isFetching` and `paused`, and no longer contains `react-query's own isLoading definition`. All three of those fail today — I grepped: isFetching appears 0 times and paused 0 times across useDashboardWidget.ts and useReport.ts, and the false phrase is present once the line break is normalized away. AC-7's check is built the same way against ReportCard.tsx, requiring `nested-interactive` and `CalendarCard`, both of which appear 0 times in that file today.

Objection 3 — qa_script step 6 is rewritten to the behaviour that actually holds. I read CalendarCard.tsx:443-461: the component-library Button carries its own onPress navigating to /reports/calendar/${widgetId}?month=YYYY-MM. A probe confirmed the card's onClick never sees that click at all — react-aria stops propagation — so the card's new guard is belt-and-braces there rather than a behaviour change, and the button navigating is correct and must be preserved. The step now asks QA to confirm navigation happens exactly once when the month label is clicked, and that the card's own goToReport does not additionally fire. risk #1 says the same thing explicitly so the implementer cannot read 'belt-and-braces' as licence to remove the button's navigate.

The click guard is the one real design decision. Finding 1's proposed `if (e.target !== e.currentTarget) return` is wrong: on a real card a user's click target is essentially never the wrapper — it is the body View, a span, or a recharts SVG node. I measured it. A guard on target identity would suppress every click that has ever worked, exactly as finding 5 says. So the guard is asymmetric with the keydown guard by necessity, not by omission: a keydown only ever starts on a focusable element so currentTarget is a meaningful comparison, whereas a click can start anywhere, so the click guard has to ask a different question — did this click land on something interactive?

Replace onClick={goToReport} with a handler that resolves event.target via closest() against an interactive-element selector — button, input, select, textarea, a[href], [contenteditable], [role="button"], [role="link"], [role="checkbox"], [role="tab"], [role="menuitem"] — and returns early when the matched element is not event.currentTarget itself. I simulated this against every real target rather than reasoning about it. Results: a plain span and the surface itself both resolve to the card and navigate; the native button and the text input resolve to themselves and block; a recharts `<rect>` resolves to the card surface (the SVG subtree contains nothing interactive) and still navigates, confirmed by an actual click reaching goToReport. The `!== currentTarget` check is load-bearing and is why the card's own role="button" does not block its own clicks — it must not be dropped.

Finding 7 is a comment edit on the block at ReportCard.tsx:113-117, which currently explains why the card is not a <Button> and stops there. Extend it to record the trade the review flagged: role="button" with tabIndex={0} around focusable descendants is itself the ARIA nested-interactive shape, the fix moved the problem from an HTML-validity error to a semantic one, and CalendarCard is the case that makes it visible.

For the test file, finding 5 is the load-bearing change and findings 4 and 6 combine into one edit of the style assertions. The positive click case currently fires on the surface, so it passes identically with or without a guard — move it to fire on screen.getByText('Balance Forecast'), a descendant. Add a native-control click case to CardWithNativeInnerControls, mirroring the keydown cases already there. Then rewrite the single style case into three over the card body rather than the surface: I read emotion's actual cascade and confirmed the body genuinely carries background-color:var(--color-tableBackground), box-shadow:0 2px 6px, and a separate .css-XXXX:hover rule with box-shadow:0 4px 6px, while the surface genuinely has no background — so all three of finding 4's claims are assertable today. Finding 6's objection is that injectedCssFor returns '' under emotion's CSSOM mode, making a not.toMatch assertion vacuously true; it does not return '' in this environment (I measured 453 characters for the surface and 728 for the body across a 4482-character cascade), but the failure mode is real and cheap to close, so each style assertion is preceded by an explicit non-empty check naming what went wrong. Keep injectedCssFor rather than deleting it: getComputedStyle cannot see a :hover state in jsdom, so the helper is the only way to make the hover claim falsifiable.

For the two hooks, apply the same change to both since they are twins. Finding 2: stop spreading. Return an explicit object — { data, error, isPending, isLoading, fetchStatus } — so status, isSuccess and isInitialLoading are no longer visible alongside a derived isPending that disagrees with them. I re-grepped every call site: twelve useDashboardWidget callers and one useReport caller, every one destructuring only data plus one of the two overridden flags, with nothing anywhere reading error, status, isSuccess, isRefetching or refetch. fetchStatus stays because both hook test files read it directly and it is the field the derivation is about. error stays because it is not one of the contradictory fields and dropping it would be an API reduction the ticket did not ask for.

Finding 3: keep the expression, fix the comment. The comment claims 'This is react-query's own isLoading definition'. queryObserver.js:310 defines isLoading as isPending && isFetching; the hook computes isPending && fetchStatus !== 'idle'. They differ in exactly one case — a paused, uncached query — and I chose the reviewer's first option rather than its second on purpose. Narrowing to isPending && query.isFetching would make a paused offline query fall out of the loading branch and render an empty report with no explanation, which is a worse outcome than a spinner for a query that is genuinely still trying and may resume. So the expression stands, the comment is corrected to say what it computes, and it states deliberately that a paused query counts as loading and why. The same fix applies to useReport.ts, which carries the comment by copy.

The hook test files each gain two cases: the comment-source assertion described above, and a not.toHaveProperty assertion that the returned object no longer carries status or isSuccess, so a future spread reappears as a failing test rather than a comment nobody reads.

The guard's `matched !== event.currentTarget` test is load-bearing: without it the card's own role="button" matches the selector and blocks every click on the card. Keep the keydown guard at lines 124-138 exactly as it is; the comment on it already explains the repeat and preventDefault ordering and must not change. Add the finding-7 trade-off paragraph to the existing comment block at lines 113-117, recording that role="button" with tabIndex={0} wrapping focusable descendants is itself the ARIA nested-interactive shape, that this change moved the defect from an HTML-validity error to a semantic one, and that CalendarCard is the case that makes it visible. The paragraph must contain the words 'nested-interactive' and 'CalendarCard' - AC-7's CI case greps for exactly those, and both are absent from the file today.

Without the click guard a native control inside a card navigates the card on click while the same control's Enter/Space is correctly left alone - I measured all four click targets reaching goToReport. The guard must not be finding 1's literal target-identity check, which I measured would suppress the plain-span and SVG clicks that are ordinary card clicks today.

Both assertions fail against the file as it stands today. (5) Import readFileSync from 'node:fs' and path from 'node:path'. files.why: Findings 4, 5 and 6, plus objection 1. The positive case as written passes identically with or without a descendant guard, so the suite cannot tell the right handler from the wrong one; the AC-5 body claims are unpinned; a silent-empty CSS read makes the one existing style assertion vacuously true; and objection 1 requires AC-7 to be provable by CI, since the schema has no review-scoped verify value.

Rewrite the comment at lines 20-24: drop 'This is react-query's own isLoading definition', state that the expression is isPending && fetchStatus !== 'idle', state that react-query's own isLoading is isPending && isFetching (queryObserver.js:310), and state that a paused query is deliberately counted as loading because it is still trying and may resume. The returned object is internally contradictory on an id-less route (isPending === false while status === 'pending' and isSuccess === false), and the comment justifying it misdescribes react-query's own semantics. The isPending && isFetching alternative was rejected because it would send a paused offline query out of the loading branch into an unexplained empty render.

risks: The click-guard selector is the one judgement call with real blast radius. Too narrow and finding 1's complaint survives for whatever control type was not listed; too broad and ordinary card clicks stop navigating. I simulated the proposed selector against every target in the real components rather than reasoning about it - a plain span and the surface resolve to the card and navigate, the native button and text input resolve to themselves and block, and a recharts <rect> resolves to the card surface and still navigates - but a custom widget body using a non-standard role could still need the selector widened. No such body is in the repo today. The closest() !== currentTarget check is what keeps the card's own role="button" from blocking itself, and it must not be dropped.

The Calendar card's own button keeps its own navigate and must not lose it. Its onPress at CalendarCard.tsx:443-461 targets /reports/calendar/${widgetId}?month=YYYY-MM, and react-aria stops propagation before the card's onClick ever sees the click, so the new guard is belt-and-braces there and changes nothing. CalendarCard is not in files[] and its behaviour is preserved by this change; qa_script step 6 is written to match that, and this risk repeats it so 'belt-and-braces' is not read as licence to remove the button's navigation.

Narrowing the hook return type is a compile-time API reduction on a shared hook. I re-grepped every call site - twelve useDashboardWidget callers plus CustomReport.tsx:66 - and none reads a dropped field, but the grep covers this repo at this commit only; anything reaching the hook dynamically would surface at typecheck, not at runtime.

The comment criteria are now enforced by tests that read source text with node:fs. That is what the review required, because the schema has no review-scoped verify value and qa.md requires a verify:'test' criterion to be CI-provable - but it is an unusual mechanism, and it couples a test to the exact wording of a comment. I mitigated that by asserting on short, distinctive tokens ('isFetching', 'paused', 'nested-interactive', 'CalendarCard') rather than whole sentences, so rewording a comment will not break the suite; a wholesale deletion of the comment still will, which is the intent. The tests import 'node:fs' into desktop-client test files, which has no precedent in that package (loot-core has it) but is legal and passes lint - no import pattern in .oxlintrc.json restricts node builtins.

Keeping 'paused' counted as loading is a deliberate choice with no test distinguishing it today. Nothing in the repo exercises an offline paused query, so if that behaviour is wrong it will not be caught by any case in tests[]. The comment records the decision so a later reader can revisit it deliberately rather than by accident.

The style assertions read emotion's injected text nodes. That is reliable in this vitest environment - I measured a 4482-character cascade, 453 characters for the surface and 728 for the body - but it is exactly the fragility finding 6 describes, and it would go silent under emotion's CSSOM mode. The added non-empty checks convert that silent pass into a loud failure, which bounds the risk rather than removing it.

React Compiler is enabled for desktop-client, so the new onClick closure is auto-memoized; this is not a concern, but the guard adds a closest() call per click on the card surface and per bubbled descendant click, which is a trivial cost on a click path.
out_of_scope: The QA finding - /reports/spending (and /reports/crossover) never finishing loading on the demo budget. The code-level reason it cannot be live is present at useDashboardWidget.ts:25 and useReport.ts:15, and the prior round tested it live in a browser and recorded both routes rendering fully on main with no console error and no failed request; QA filed it against the PR before that fix landed. Dropped per the issue body's own instruction to drop findings that do not hold up, not deferred. qa_script step 8 re-checks it anyway so a regression is caught.

Renaming PR #26 to carry the mandatory [AI] prefix (finding 8). It is a merged pull request, not a file change, and .github/** is a forbidden path. This is a human action on GitHub, not work this ticket can carry.

Replacing role="button" with a semantically correct nested-interactive structure. Finding 7 asks only that the trade be recorded, and doing the actual a11y restructure would change the click target and accessible name that the e2e selectors depend on - a much larger change than this follow-up ticket.

Any behaviour change to the keydown path. Finding 3's second option (narrowing isFirstLoad to isPending && query.isFetching) was considered and rejected: it would push a paused offline query out of the loading branch into an unexplained empty render.

Editing injectedCssFor into a CSSOM-capable reader, or widening its class-matching regex beyond the bare substring test finding 6 objects to. The non-empty guards close the failure mode finding 6 actually names; making the helper CSSOM-safe is a separate change that would ship on its own.

A release note in upcoming-release-notes/. No user-visible behaviour changes: the click-guard fix removes a latent path that is unreachable today (finding 1 says so explicitly), the hook change is a type-level narrowing with no runtime effect, and the rest are comments and test assertions. A note for this would ship on its own and say nothing.
work_order.confidence_rationale: This is a replan against three review objections, and I answered each one by running code rather than by re-arguing it. Objection 1 asked whether a verify:"test" criterion could be CI-provable; I read .sdlc/schemas/work-order.json's verify enum (browser|test|api — there is no "review", so the reviewer's option (a) is not available) and qa.md:222-224, then built and ran the mechanism option (b) depends on: a throwaway probe proved that readFileSync(new URL('./X.tsx', import.meta.url)) throws "The URL must be of scheme file" under this vitest setup, while path.resolve(import.meta.dirname, './X.tsx') and a process.cwd()-relative path both resolve and read the file's real content. The work order specifies the form that works, so the implementer does not have to discover it. Objection 2 claimed AC-5's grep was vacuous; I confirmed the phrase is split across useDashboardWidget.ts:22-23 and that isFetching and paused appear zero times in either hook today, so the replacement assertions fail on unmodified code and pass only after the comment is rewritten. Objection 3 claimed qa_script step 6 contradicted CalendarCard; I read CalendarCard.tsx:443-461 and confirmed the component-library Button's own onPress navigates to /reports/calendar/<widgetId>?month=YYYY-MM, and a probe confirmed the card's onClick never sees that click (react-aria stops propagation), so the step is rewritten to assert navigation happens exactly once, via the button. Beyond the objections I re-verified the substance the objections rested on: a probe clicked five targets and measured that the native button, a plain span, a text input and the surface all reach goToReport today (the guard gap is real), simulated the proposed selector against every target (span and surface resolve to the card itself and navigate; native button and input resolve to themselves and block; a recharts <rect> resolves to the card surface and still navigates), and read emotion's injected cascade to confirm all three of finding 4's claims are assertable today (body carries background-color:var(--color-tableBackground), box-shadow 0 2px 6px, and a separate :hover rule with 0 4px 6px, while the surface carries no background). The 20 existing tests in the three affected files pass at this commit. Confidence is 90 rather than higher for two judgement calls that remain genuinely open: the breadth of the interactive selector, and whether asserting on comment text via node:fs is a mechanism the maintainers would rather review by eye — objection 1 explicitly called option (b) the safer default, and I have followed it, but a council may still prefer the comment claims folded into a code assertion.
evidence: Baseline: yarn workspace @actual-app/web run test on ReportCard.test.tsx, useDashboardWidget.test.tsx and useReport.test.tsx passes 20 tests in 3 files at this commit. That is the fence the change must not break.

Objection 1 answered: .sdlc/schemas/work-order.json's acceptance.verify enum is [browser, test, api] - there is no review-scoped value, so the reviewer's option (a) is unavailable and option (b) is the only route. .sdlc/agents/qa.md:222-224 confirms a verify:'test' criterion is proven by CI and must cite 'ci' in test_ids, and qa.md:224 makes verdict pass impossible while any AC is not_covered.

Objection 1 answered by running the mechanism: a probe calling readFileSync(new URL('./ReportCard.tsx', import.meta.url), 'utf8') under this vitest setup fails with 'TypeError: The URL must be of scheme file'. path.resolve(import.meta.dirname, 'ReportCard.tsx') resolves and its content contains role="button" (existsSync true), as does a process.cwd()-relative path. The work order specifies the import.meta.dirname form.

Objection 2 answered: the offending phrase is split across packages/desktop-client/src/hooks/useDashboardWidget.ts:22-23 by a line break and a `//` marker, so a grep for the joined phrase matches nothing on the unmodified tree - the old AC-5 check could not fail. grep confirms 'isFetching' appears 0 times and 'paused' 0 times across useDashboardWidget.ts and useReport.ts, and 'nested-interactive' and 'CalendarCard' appear 0 times in ReportCard.tsx, so every replacement assertion fails on today's code and passes only after the comment is rewritten.

Objection 3 answered by reading the code: packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/reports/CalendarCard.tsx:443-461 gives the month Button an onPress navigating to /reports/calendar/${widgetId}?month=YYYY-MM, and CalendarCard renders that inside ReportCard at 165-171. The button navigating is therefore intended, and the old qa_script step 6 asked QA to confirm the opposite. A probe confirms the card's onClick never receives that click - clicking the component-library Button produced exactly one navigate call, its own - because react-aria stops propagation, so the card's guard is belt-and-braces there and the button's behaviour is unchanged by this work order.

Finding 1's guard gap re-verified by probe: clicking a plain span, a native <button>, a text <input> and the surface each produced exactly one navigate call to '/reports/net-worth' with state {goBack:true}. Every descendant click reaches goToReport today.

Finding 5 verified, and it is why finding 1 cannot be implemented as written: simulating the proposed closest() selector over the real components gives span -> the card surface (navigates), surface -> itself (navigates), native button -> itself (blocked), text input -> itself (blocked), component-library Button -> itself (blocked, though react-aria already prevents it arriving), and a recharts <rect> -> the card surface, with an actual click on the rect reaching goToReport. A strict e.target !== e.currentTarget guard would suppress the span and the rect, which are ordinary card clicks.

Finding 4 verified as assertable today by reading emotion's injected cascade: the card body's rule carries background-color:var(--color-tableBackground) and box-shadow:0 2px 6px rgba(0, 0, 0, .15), and a separate rule '.css-w4wco7:hover{box-shadow:0 4px 6px rgba(0, 0, 0, .15);}' carries the hover deepening; the click surface's own rule matches no background declaration at all. theme.tableBackground resolves to 'var(--color-tableBackground)', so the assertion should compare against the token rather than a hardcoded string.

Finding 6's premise checked and found to be a latent risk rather than a live failure here: the cascade read 4482 characters, 453 for the surface and 728 for the body, so emotion is writing text nodes under vitest, not the CSSOM. The silent-empty failure mode is still real under speedy mode, so the plan keeps the helper and adds explicit non-empty checks.

Finding 3 verified against the installed library: @tanstack/query-core 5.101.2 queryObserver.js:310 defines isLoading as isPending && isFetching, with isFetching computed as fetchStatus === 'fetching'. The hook computes isPending && fetchStatus !== 'idle' and its comment claims the former. The comment is false.

Finding 2 verified by enumerating consumers: twelve useDashboardWidget call sites (AgeOfMoney, BalanceForecast, BudgetAnalysis, Calendar, CashFlow, Crossover, Formula, NetWorth, Sankey, Spending, Summary, monte-carlo/MonteCarlo) and one useReport call site (CustomReport.tsx:66, imported as useCustomReport). Every one destructures only data plus one of the two overridden flags. Both hook test files read result.current.fetchStatus directly, which is why fetchStatus stays on the narrowed type.

The existing suites encode the behaviour the hook change must preserve: useReport.test.tsx and useDashboardWidget.test.tsx each have three cases (bare route with no id, first load resolving, staying loaded through a background refetch over cached data), and the refetch case's own comment - 'Deriving the flag from fetchStatus alone would put a spinner back here on every navigation to a report' - is why the isFirstLoad override must not be simplified away.

The QA finding's code-level reason for not reproducing is present on main: useDashboardWidget.ts:20-27 and useReport.ts:12-17 both carry the isFirstLoad override with the disabled-query explanation, and an id-less route is exactly the case it exists for (enabled: !!id && !!type is false). The prior round of this plan tested it live and recorded both routes rendering fully; I did not re-run the browser this round and say so rather than implying otherwise.

alternatives_considered.approach: Answer objection 1 with option (a): set AC-5 and AC-7 to verify: "review", on the assumption that some review-scoped value exists.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It does not. The review told me to check rather than choose from memory, and I did: .sdlc/schemas/work-order.json's verify enum is exactly [browser, test, api], so "review" would fail schema validation and the whole work order would be rejected unread. Option (b) - real CI cases - is the only remaining route, and the review named it the safer default for the same reason.

alternatives_considered.approach: Implement finding 1 literally: add if (e.target !== e.currentTarget) return to onClick, exactly as proposed.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: A regression, and finding 5 says so. I measured four click targets all reaching goToReport: native button, plain span, text input and surface. A target-identity guard suppresses the first three, so a plain click on a chart label or a body span - what a user actually does - would stop opening the report. I also confirmed a recharts <rect> reaches goToReport. That is precisely the state the retargeted positive case exists to prevent.

alternatives_considered.approach: Write the source-reading tests with the idiomatic readFileSync(new URL('./X.tsx', import.meta.url), 'utf8').
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It throws. I ran it: TypeError: The URL must be of scheme file, because this vitest setup does not give the test module a file-scheme URL usable that way. The work order specifies path.resolve(import.meta.dirname, ...) instead, which I verified reads the file's real content. Left as-is it would have cost the implementer a debugging round.

alternatives_considered.approach: Keep onClick unguarded and instead wrap every interactive control in a widget body with its own stopPropagation, the way react-aria's Button already does.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It pushes the burden onto every future widget body, and the bodies are third-party-ish render code (recharts, CalendarGraph) rather than code this change owns. ReportCard is the single place that knows the rule, so the rule belongs there - which is also what finding 1 asks for, minus the wrong predicate.

alternatives_considered.approach: Delete injectedCssFor and assert the body styling some other way (finding 6 offers this).
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: getComputedStyle cannot resolve a :hover state in jsdom - a hover state does not exist there - so removing the helper makes the hover-deepening claim unassertable, which is one of the three claims finding 4 exists to pin. Keeping the helper with explicit non-empty guards takes finding 6's actual objection (silent emptiness) while preserving finding 4's requirement.

alternatives_considered.approach: For finding 2, keep the spread and instead derive status and isSuccess to agree with the overridden isPending.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It makes the object agree by asserting something false - status would be 'success' on a route that has never fetched. A narrowed type is the honest fix: it makes the contradiction unrepresentable rather than papering over it.

alternatives_considered.approach: For finding 3, narrow the expression to isPending && query.isFetching so the existing comment becomes true and the isLoading override is exactly redundant.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It changes behaviour in the one case the two expressions differ, and changes it for the worse. A paused query with no cached data (offline, first visit) would leave the loading branch and render an empty report with no explanation, where today it spins. The reviewer's first option - say what the expression actually is and keep 'paused' deliberately - is correct here, so the comment is what changes.

alternatives_considered.approach: Reopen the QA defect and plan a fix for the infinite spinner.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: There is no defect on main to fix. The isFirstLoad override the id-less routes depend on is present at useDashboardWidget.ts:25 and useReport.ts:15, and the prior round confirmed both routes render fully in the browser on the demo budget. Planning work against a bug that cannot be reproduced would produce a change with no failing case and no way to verify it - and the issue body explicitly warns against 'implementing something that was never wrong'.

unknowns: Whether asserting on comment text via node:fs is a mechanism the maintainers will accept long-term. The review required it as the only route to a CI-provable verify:'test' criterion, and I have minimised the coupling by asserting on short tokens rather than sentences, but a council may prefer to fold the comment claims into a code-level assertion instead. That is a question about how the work order is checked, not about what it changes.

Whether the paused-query loading behaviour should be pinned by a test. Nothing in the repo exercises it, so the choice made here (keep 'paused' as loading) is recorded in a comment rather than by a case. If review wants it pinned, it needs a query client configured with networkMode: 'offlineFirst' or an equivalent, which I did not attempt.

Whether an interactive element type exists in a widget body that the selector does not cover. I covered every natively interactive element plus the ARIA interactive roles the bodies use, and simulated the selector against every target in the existing components; a custom widget body using a non-standard role could still need it widened.

Whether finding 6's underlying concern - emotion switching to CSSOM mode - can occur in this repo's vitest configuration at all. It does not at this commit; the non-empty guards make the question moot either way, but I did not trace why text mode is selected here.

Whether the ReportCard-versus-hooks split of findings should be two tickets. I judged one work order correct on file count and shared origin; if the council disagrees, the split is clean because the two groups touch disjoint files.
